span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The task set tunes unconscious processing: a category task desensitizes the pathways coding prime elongation while a shape task, needing only attention to basic visual features, sensitizes them and so lets the priming effect emerge
span.note: status: the paper's own words: Speculative
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Attentional sensitization by task set raises the sensitivity of task-relevant pathways and lowers that of task-irrelevant ones, which is the process offered for why priming appears in one task and not the other
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The width/length ratio distribution differed across categories and was not modelled as a random effect, so it may have driven the shape-task priming.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Primes also appeared as visible targets, so stimulus-response mapping cannot be excluded as an explanation of the priming effects.

span.label: **A NULL AND AN EFFECT IN ONE SENTENCE, WHICH IS WHY THE NULL CANNOT BE DISMISSED:** `we found EVIDENCE FOR PRIMING IN A SHAPE TASK, but NONE FOR PRIMING IN A CATEGORY TASK, when prime stimuli were rendered invisible using CFS.` **The corpus's second powered priming null after bamberger2024, and a stronger one** - there the whole result was a null and the authors had to name reasons the manipulation might have failed. Here the null is HALF OF A WITHIN-PAPER CONTRAST: same primes, same suppression, same subjects, and the other task showed the effect. A failed manipulation cannot produce that
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE CONCLUSION IS A RESTRICTION ON A METHOD THE FIELD HAS BEEN EXPANDING:** `Quotation withheld.` The introduction records that CFS has been called a `game changer` for its `seemingly unlimited potential to present various kinds of visual stimuli unconsciously`. **This paper is the counter-pressure**, and the corpus should hold the claim and its limit together rather than one of them
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THEY DECLINE TO OVER-READ THE POSITIVE HALF, WHICH IS RARER THAN REPORTING THE NULL:** `Quotation withheld.` The effect they DID find does not fit the obvious account. **Most records in this corpus defend their surviving result; this one reports that its own is unexplained** - which is what makes the null beside it credible
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE MECHANISM OFFERED IS MARKED AS SPECULATION INSIDE ITS OWN SENTENCE:** `SPECULATIVELY, the category task might have DESENSITIZED perceptual pathways related to the processing of prime elongation and thus diminished category-by-shape priming; by contrast, the shape task - requiring only attention to basic visual features - SENSITIZED perceptual pathways.` Attentional sensitization as a TASK-SET effect (Kiefer 2012). **If it holds, every masked-priming null in the literature is conditional on the task used to measure it** - which would make the measurement instrument part of the phenomenon, and is the strongest version of what this corpus keeps finding one record at a time
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: CFS —causes→ priming
span.note: direction on the measure: no-change · strength of the relation: 0.9 — **`no-change` ON THE CATEGORY TASK, AND THE SHAPE TASK IS THE CONTROL THAT MAKES IT MEAN SOMETHING.** The same quote carries both halves: priming survives suppression in one task and not the other. Recording only the surviving half would say CFS leaves priming intact; recording only the null would say it abolishes it; **both are wrong and the sentence says so.** Q-801's ambiguity does not arise - the measured quantity and the construct move together - but Q-804's does: the direction is conditioned on the task, and there is no way to say that on an edge. Weight 0.9.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: shape task —contrasted-with→ category task
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — **THE CONTRAST IS THE RESULT.** Not two tasks compared for their own sake - the difference between them IS the finding, because it is what turns a null into evidence about the level of representation that survives suppression rather than evidence about the experiment. Weight 0.95: explicit in the quote and it is the paper's title.

span.label: With the same stimuli and the same observers, a shape-discrimination task did produce priming: shape-congruent primes speeded responses to elongated tool targets, with a reversed and less robust difference for nonelongated tool targets.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Across both experiments there is no support for unconscious category-by-shape priming under CFS, but suppressed prime shape does affect shape discrimination of tool targets.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The primes were genuinely invisible: forced-choice category discrimination of primes rated invisible was at chance level, 48.87% in Experiment 1.

span.label: The pattern is read as evidence that stimuli suppressed by CFS are represented only as features and coarse feature configurations, not at a category or semantic level.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Because earlier studies used only elongated tool targets and only nonelongated animal targets, participants in those studies could have solved the task by shape rather than by category, which would explain their apparent category priming.
